clue.text: Proper way of approaching revolutionary quarter?

parts.note: proper means right, as in the right thing to do
an angle is a way of approaching a subject, as a journalist's angle on a story

explanation.surface: A question about the correct manner of entering a district run by revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests politics, but a quarter of a full revolution is a ninety-degree turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A full turn is 360 degrees, so a quarter of one is the 90-degree corner of a square.

clue.text: Revolutionary sort of tyre incorporating carbon

indicators.note: incorporating means the tyre word takes the next piece into its body

parts.note: a radial is a kind of tyre with radially laid cords
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A new kind of tyre with carbon in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical seeks sweeping political change, as a revolutionary does.

clue.text: Getting it into the net, I manage by myself

indicators.note: into means the word it is put inside the net word

parts.note: the net in football is the goal
I and one both stand for a single person

explanation.surface: A footballer boasts of scoring without help from teammates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' is a link here; 'I' is read as ONE, a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: To go it alone is an idiom for acting independently, without help.

clue.text: Bite cake thus? It is cooked to surpass all others

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or altered, so the letters before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cake is bitten, and the baker asks whether it is done.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'It' look like a new sentence, but 'It' simply follows the rearranged letters of 'Bite cake thus'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be the most remarkable, beating everything else.

clue.text: Make invalid fill one up before end of surgery

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written
'un is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good 'un'

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An instruction to cancel a filling before the surgery closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FILL UN to NULLIF; Y then comes from the last letter of 'surgery'.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify is to cancel the force of something, making it void.

clue.text: In Dublin see damask, a product of flax

indicators.note: In at the front says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Damask cloth seen in Dublin, made from flax.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed is the seed of the flax plant, pressed for oil.

clue.text: Protection for low joint in a quarrel

definitions.meaning: a gaiter covering the ankle and the top of the shoe

explanation.surface: Something guards an ankle during a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an ankle covering worn over a shoe, and a minor row.

clue.text: Stab with a knife

parts.note: a stab of pain is a pang

explanation.surface: Someone is stabbed with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A panga is a large broad-bladed African knife like a machete.

clue.text: More drunk, forgetting one small thing

indicators.note: forgetting means a piece is left out

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk, so more drunk is tiddlier
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A drinker gets tipsier and forgets one small item.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiddler is a very small fish or child, anything little.

clue.text: Sceptic, but ordered into action with poet

indicators.note: into places the rearranged word inside the action word

parts.note: doing is action, as in deeds

indicators.note: ordered means the word is put into a new order

parts.note: Dylan Thomas, the Welsh poet

explanation.surface: A doubter is nevertheless pushed into action alongside a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns BUT into UBT, which goes into DOING.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Thomas doubted the resurrection, so his epithet names any habitual doubter.

clue.text: Dark liquid given by doctor to swallow

parts.note: ink is the dark fluid used for writing

explanation.surface: A doctor hands over a dark medicine for the patient to take down.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink is to take liquid down the throat, which is swallowing it.

clue.text: Where the first-born went to sleep

definitions.meaning: in Genesis Cain, Adam and Eve's first-born son, went to dwell in the land east of Eden after killing Abel
a jocular name for the state of slumber

explanation.surface: The eldest child went off to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first-born' reads as any eldest child, but it is Cain, Adam's first son.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical place of Cain's exile is also a playful idiom for being asleep.

clue.text: Sectional organisation in seaside area

indicators.note: organisation here means arranging, so the letters of the word before are reordered

explanation.surface: A sectional body is set up in a resort district.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoreline strip where land meets sea is the area at the seaside.

clue.text: Shout loudly, to contain resistance in fight

indicators.note: to contain means the shouting word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: to bawl is to shout loudly
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone yells loudly to keep opposition in check during a scuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a rough, noisy fight, a punch-up.

clue.text: Vaguely see battle at the front

parts.note: Loos was a 1915 First World War battle on the Western Front
Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see

explanation.surface: A soldier dimly makes out the fighting at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese, here Ely in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something loosely means without precision, which is vaguely.

clue.text: Chink in the German boat

indicators.note: in tells us the crack sits inside the German article

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a chink is a narrow crack or rift

explanation.surface: There is a crack in the hull of the German vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a fishing boat that uses drift nets.

clue.text: What leaders come to, taking note accordingly

indicators.note: taking means the phrase takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: leaders come to the fore, the front
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Bosses end up taking notes as required.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore and accordingly both mean as a consequence.

clue.text: He's rich, rolling in treasure

indicators.note: rolling means the letters turn over into a new order

explanation.surface: A wealthy man is rolling in valuables.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure someone or something is to hold it dear.

clue.text: "Excellent', I say

parts.note: an old-fashioned British exclamation of approval, said when something pleases

explanation.surface: Someone gives a hearty word of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation the word was dated British slang for first-rate.

clue.text: One runs a long way from bird of prey

definitions.meaning: a hawk that hunts low over open ground

explanation.surface: Something flees a long way from a hawk.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a cross-country runner and a slim hawk.

clue.text: Way to enlist, for example, soldiers in division

indicators.note: to enlist is to take in or recruit, so the way word holds the rest

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
EG is short for exempli gratia, for example
men is a usual crossword word for soldiers

explanation.surface: A route to recruit troops into an army division.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one part of a whole, a division of it.

clue.text: Scornfully refused to drive Edward

parts.note: to spur is to drive or urge on
Ned is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone contemptuously declined to give Edward a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn is to reject with contempt.

clue.text: Touching explosive without a lot of irritation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the explosive goes round

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: anger is irritation

explanation.surface: An explosive device without much fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside'; 'a lot of' drops the final letter of the irritation word, and the explosive wraps round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a tangent line touches a curve at one point.

clue.text: Lose one's bottle in the grass

definitions.meaning: British slang: to lose one's nerve, bottle meaning courage
a kind of millet grass of the genus Panicum

explanation.surface: Someone loses a bottle in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'bottle' means courage, so losing it is losing nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's nerve is a fit of fear; the grass name is a botanical sense.

clue.text: Coming up, for instance, in an African lake

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards
in puts the example word inside the article

parts.note: say means for instance

explanation.surface: Something rising, for example, in an African lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming up' suits a down clue: the whole assembly is read from the bottom, the example word sitting inside the article first.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyasa is the old name of Lake Malawi in East Africa.

clue.text: Crudely formed — when?

parts.note: done crudely means done rough

indicators.note: formed means the letters of the next word are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks at what time a rough shape was made.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and also builds: ROUGH from 'Crudely' plus HEWN, the letters of 'when' rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something roughly chopped into shape with an axe is crudely made, not finished.

clue.text: Long-established custom in Tennessee — wireless covers it

indicators.note: in places the material inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: TN is the postal abbreviation for Tennessee

indicators.note: covers means the wireless word goes round the next piece

parts.note: wireless is an old word for radio

explanation.surface: An old custom in Tennessee involves the radio covering a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wireless' is the old British word for a radio set.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a custom handed down over generations.

clue.text: Low points for deer

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: Weak spots for a stag.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is the largest species of deer.

clue.text: Advance, with no company to speak of

indicators.note: to speak of signals that the word is said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: lone means alone, with nobody else

explanation.surface: An advance made by a firm that hardly exists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to speak of' looks like the idiom for 'worth mentioning', but signals a soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance of money is a sum lent, to be paid back.

clue.text: Displaying many colours in one' New England state by fall

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island
a descent is a fall or drop

explanation.surface: Autumn leaves in a New England state show many colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' reads as the American autumn, fitting New England, but it is a descent.
explanation.definitionFit: An iridescent surface shimmers with changing rainbow hues.
